value: Sec. 37.2(h): an owner, lessor, sublessor who receives rent, and the agent, representative or successor
detail: No distinction between a corporation, an LLC, a trust and an individual property owner. Every landlord of a covered unit is subject to the same Chapter 37 limits.

value: Large owners and small owners face the identical 1.6% allowable annual increase, the 12-month rule, and the Sec. 37.15 license requirement
detail: The Rent Ordinance and the Housing Inventory rules are written in terms of 'owners' and 'landlords', not entity size or type.

value: Buildings with 10+ residential units: reporting from July 1, 2022. Condominiums and buildings with fewer than 10 units: from March 1, 2023
detail: This is the only size-based distinction in the official licensing rules; it is a building-size rule, not a corporate-status rule.

value: Bulk Housing Inventory uploads are offered for properties with 5 or more units; a property manager/agent may be designated for habitability contacts
detail: Small owners are directed to the Portal's 'Individual Unit' submission form instead of the Excel template.

value: AB 1482's single-family-home / condo exemption is NOT available if the owner is a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member
detail: Civil Code 1947.12(d)(5)(A) and the SF Rent Board's AB 1482 page. This is the clearest official corporation-vs-individual difference found. It does not apply to units covered by SF rent control.

value: Any landlord (corporate or individual) seeking more than the annual/banked amount must file a Rent Board petition with supporting documentation BEFORE serving the notice
detail: Six petition categories; no filing charge; tenants need not pay until the Rent Board approves. Rule 6.10 requires actual costs and proof of payment for O&M petitions.

topic: Internal corporate pricing practices, algorithms, renewal software, portfolio-wide increase policies
detail: No official government source describing how large real-estate corporations set or implement rent increases was located. Value intentionally left blank and flagged unverified; commercial blogs and press reports were deliberately excluded because they are not official sources.

topic: Practical routine for a small owner
value: Report into the Housing Inventory by March 1; pay the Rent Board fee; confirm the license; apply the published rate on each unit's anniversary date; serve a compliant written notice; keep records
detail: All six steps are individually verified on the Rent Board Process and Requirements pages. This is an editorial synthesis, not a quoted instruction.

value: Rent Board counseling is free for landlords as well as tenants, but counselors cannot give legal advice
detail: The City also lists landlord resources: SF Apartment Association and Small Property Owners of San Francisco (membership organizations), plus Bar Association of San Francisco conflict-intervention services.

topic: Written notice; personal delivery or mail
value: Civil Code 827(b)(1): deliver a copy personally or serve by mail under Code of Civil Procedure 1013
detail: sf.gov adds 5 days to the notice period when the notice is mailed (e.g., 35 days instead of 30).

value: Measured alone or combined with any other increase in the preceding 12 months
detail: Civil Code 827(b)(2)-(3)(A); confirmed by sf.gov.
sf.gov's notice checklist. For banked increases, also state which part is banked and the dates on which the banked amount is based.
value: Required in the written notice

topic: Break out each component of the increase
value: Annual / banked / capital improvement / O&M / utility / RAP loan portions must be identified
detail: Sec. 37.3(b)(1)-(4) and Rule 4.10(a). 'Any rent increase which does not conform with the provisions of this section shall be null and void.'

value: NO - the license does not need to be included with the rent increase notice
detail: It must simply be on file and current on the effective date.

topic: Official model notice / template wording for a rent increase notice
detail: The Rent Board publishes a notice-content checklist and petition forms, but no official model rent-increase notice template was located. Value intentionally left blank and flagged. Do not invent wording; have counsel or a Rent Board counselor review the draft.

value: No justification or petition is required
detail: Form 571: an owner may increase base rent once every 12 months by the allowable amount 'without filing a petition at the Rent Board'. The notice-content checklist does not include a statement of reasons. The reason is simply the City's annually published rate applied on the anniversary date.

value: Previously skipped allowable annual increases, with the years/dates identified in the notice
detail: A lawful, documented reason for a larger one-time increase, but it requires exact arithmetic, the banked breakdown, and 90-day notice if the total exceeds 10%. The 12/24-month conflict is flagged.

value: Capital improvements, increased operating & maintenance expenses, comparable rents, utility passthroughs, Proposition I rent history - all require a Rent Board petition and supporting documentation
detail: Rule 6.10 requires actual costs and proof of payment; Rule 6.12(a) allows denial where a tenant's ordinary repair requests were not performed. 'Rising costs' alone is not a lawful basis for exceeding the cap without a petition.

value: After paying the fee in full, 50% may be recovered from a qualifying tenant ($29.50 per dwelling unit for 2026-2027)
detail: Separate from base rent; cannot be used as a base for the percentage calculation.

value: A new or additional roommate/occupant, or a change in who lives in the unit while an original occupant remains
detail: Sec. 37.3(a)(11)(A), Rule 6.13, and Sec. 37.3(d)(2)(B). Any agreement to pay more is void and unenforceable. Directly relevant to Unit 1.

value: Retaliation or a protected characteristic
detail: Government Code 12955(f) prohibits retaliation; 42 USC 3604(b) prohibits discriminatory rental terms; the SF Human Rights Commission receives these complaints.

value: Any tenant may challenge an increase with a free petition, and there is NO TIME LIMIT for filing an unlawful-rent-increase petition
detail: The Rent Board holds an ALJ hearing with evidence and cross-examination, issues a written decision, and permits appeal. A tenant need not have a lawyer.

value: San Francisco's Tenant Right to Counsel program provides free legal assistance for residents facing eviction; the City directs tenants to the Eviction Defense Collaborative
detail: Official City notice: 'You are eligible for free assistance through the Tenant Right to Counsel Program.' MOHCD: the 2018 No Eviction Without Representation Act established the program. sf.gov lists free legal help at (415) 659-9184.

value: The City lists tenant counseling organizations for rent increase notices, and the Rent Board publishes a referral listing of advocacy and legal organizations
detail: Includes Housing Rights Committee of SF, SF Tenants Union, Bay Area Legal Aid, Legal Assistance to the Elderly, and Open Door Legal's Sunset office at 1722 Irving Street, San Francisco, CA 94122. The Rent Board explicitly does not handle discrimination/retaliation.

topic: What a tenant-side lawyer will test first
value: Coverage; current license on the effective date; correct base rent; rate in effect on the effective date; one increase per 12 months; 30/90-day notice and contents; banked arithmetic; no extra charge for new occupants; no discrimination/retaliation
detail: ANALYSIS derived from the official challenge grounds, notice rules and petition instructions. Not a quoted official checklist. Each underlying item has its own verified row on the Requirements page.

topic: Will a tenant lawyer necessarily approve a 1.6% increase?
detail: No official source can guarantee the outcome of an advocate's or lawyer's review; that is a legal opinion, not a verifiable fact. Value intentionally left blank and flagged unverified. The design target is that every requirement is documented and independently checkable.

value: License confirmation for the effective date; the Form 571 rate for that date; the written calculation on base rent; proof of service of the notice; a written, uniformly applied increase policy; the lease and rent history
detail: ANALYSIS (editorial recommendation). Tenant petitions ask for the lease, notices, receipts and prior Rent Board decisions; the Portal is the official license check.
